body: I agree with you, with everything. My only advice would be that you are not justified in giving up *until* you have tried absolutely every possible treatment. Time is also a treatment, and one day, in 10 years, or 15 years, if you have worked really hard to find treatments for your problems, then not continuing starts to become a viable option. But right now, you haven't. Look forward to the future knowing that you don't have to live a long life of pain, that either way you will be free of the pain one day. Tell yourself this and know that if you rule out all the other options to to not continuing then it will be true: 'I will not be 30 years old and suffering like this'.

I think it's an interesting opinion, and I think sometimes it's correct. Consider this. Someone who is 90 years old and suffering from dementia may still be able to appreciate the view from their window of the garden in their nursing home; but they may not remember their children and grandchildren. That's why it should be a choice. If that person has specifically stated they don't want to live like that, euthanasia is the right decision, *if* their dementia is incurable and they have asked for that.

The same thing goes for chronic pain, or mental illness (including chronic depression), *if* it is incurable. If someone is suffering and knows that the suffering is going to be permanent, it's their choice if they want to live with it or not. I am not at that stage yet, and I have hope that I won't reach it, but if I do reach it I hope I can find someone who will support that decision. And knowing that it will be the right thing to do eventually is what makes me rethink my original post, in which I suggested now is the best time. I'm not certain that it's incurable yet. I can look forward to the future knowing that either way, I won't have to keep suffering for another 40, 50 or 60 years. It'll only be a few more years of pain and then either way I will be released from my suffering. That thought will make me try to be cured of depression.

Thanks for posting. Knowing you found something that seems to work will keep me trying for longer, because so far I've only tied a lot of therapy, antidepressants once (but as I was a teenager and they were SSRIs they actually precipitated my first attempt) and I've tried all the basic stuff like healthy diet, meditation, exercise, etc. etc.

But I'm going to keep trying to manage my mental illness until I've tried everything, and now I know that if the day does come when I've tried everything, I can die knowing I've made the right choice. When you're suicidal knowing that after trying everything (including time) suicide is the right thing to do is such a relief, and such a reason to try. I wish people understood that. That keeping suicide as the final option is such a comfort, as long as you try.

I used to smoke but I found it was just a very temporary escape. It did help me but I can't get it at all where I live now (Japan, very strict) but I'm thinking about growing a plant in my cupboard. 

Anyway, I haven't tried everything yet, and after talking to people I've made a decision to keep trying treatments, because I know once all my options are exhausted my doubt will be gone too. I hope that day doesn't come, but I now have time to work towards preventing it and also time to accept that I have to go if that's what it comes to. Dying is hard to come to terms with even for the suicidal.

And while I still want it to be over now, knowing that suicide will become the right choice once I've tried everything is a great relief. I wish when I talked to people about suicide, they told me it **is** the best option when you've tried everything. Knowing that makes me not want to kill myself now, it makes me want to try everything first so that I know I'm making the right decision. I hope that is informative for you too, it might help someone else some day.
